articles.title: 'It might be time to wrap it up' - O'Neill ponders Celtic future after defeat
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill says he will use the international break to reflect on his position after Celtic suffer three consecutive defeats in big games.
articles.body:
He delivered a double few thought possible last season when the Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup were salvaged from the potential wreckage of one of Celtic's most tumultuous seasons.

He very nearly lifted the Uefa Cup in 2003 against a Jose Mourinho-inspired Porto who, the following season, won the Champions League.

His status as one of the club's all-time great managers is surely secure.

Which is perhaps why, so soon after returning to the club as its unlikely saviour, manager Martin O'Neill wondered out loud whether now, at the age of 74, it's finally time "to wrap it up".

The Northern Irishman's words came in the post-match news conference following a second defeat in a week against arch-rivals Rangers.

The fact he also joked about being "110 years old in two years' time" ought not to deflect from the fact O'Neill might now be seriously considering whether he's still the right man to be in charge of Celtic.

Celtic suffer second derby defeat by Rangers in week

Watch: Scott Brown & Andy Halliday discuss Old Firm game on YouTube

Rangers look like they know where they want to go - Celtic just look lost

After such a damaging week, with a home European defeat to Ferencvaros in-between the two losses to Rangers, might O'Neill decide to protect his fine legacy at the club by walking away while the side is still top of the Premiership?

"I genuinely will reflect and see," he said. "It's a matter of whether I can help the team. The manager is supposed to be able to do that. I will look at that this week.

"I think every single time something crops up and things don't go so well, age plays a part. And, do you know what, they might be right. I'll be 110 in two years' time so it might be time to wrap it up.

"I will reflect on the games and speak to the board. You never know, they may well want to speak to me. I'll try to get a couple of days away and see how it goes. "

Lending credence to the notion that O'Neill is about to embark on a period of proper soul-searching, he referenced last season's dramatic last-day decider in which Celtic won the title in the last few minutes of the final league game.

"The game against Hearts was probably one of the great moments of my managerial time. And I've had some really good moments," he added.

"While that was good and I was delighted to get that opportunity, all the time I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy and the desire - the things that I say to the boys every Friday - so I'll have a look at that and we'll see."

It's worth remembering that half an hour into the second leg of their Champions League play-off in August, Celtic were 4-0 up on aggregate against LASK in Linz and seemingly cruising to the league phase of European football's elite competition.

The collapse within that game - and the humiliating exit from the competition - seems to have left an indelible scar on the players and management team alike.

The four Premiership wins that followed were largely unimpressive; three of them single-goal victories against Falkirk, St Mirren and St Johnstone. When the pressure was on against Rangers - twice - and Ferencvaros, Celtic simply folded.

Questions have been asked by a section of the club's support about the quality, breadth and timing of the recent summer recruitment.

Former Scotland international James McFadden remains unconvinced. "They haven't actually added to the squad in terms of numbers or real quality," he said on Sky Sports. "They've just replaced what left."

O'Neill has tried to find a way to accommodate big-money signings Camilo Duran and Kasper Hogh into the side, without much success. He has tried a series of different midfielders to try to reinvigorate the heart of his team.

O'Neill even tried dropping his wingers entirely in Sunday's league derby, fielding five defenders and pushing full-back Kieran Tierney further forward. All to no avail.

Chris Sutton, who played under O'Neill during the manager's first spell at the club, was deeply unimpressed by what he saw.

"It wasn't a close game," he said on Sky Sports. "There was a massive gulf. I can't remember a Celtic team getting such a doing from a Rangers team at Celtic Park.

"Rangers were a team and Celtic weren't. They knew their next pass and Celtic didn't. Rangers were better in every department. They were smashed and that's the concern.

"They have big problems, some self-inflicted. They've lacked legs and physicality in the middle of the park. This has been a big issue all season. Callum McGregor's another year older, can't get about the pitch like he used to.

"Martin will have to come up with something. I loved him as a manager when I was at the club. He is getting on a bit but, as a guy, I still think he has the fight for it."

That sentiment is shared by Sutton's former team-mate, Neil Lennon, who knows O'Neill better than most and who also knows how heavily the mantle of Celtic manager can weigh.

"He's hurting, he's smarting about it," Lennon said on Sky Sports. "He'd want to find the answers. The break's come at a good time for him - recuperate, get some sun and re-think about the whole thing. He still feels he's got the energy to do it."

"When you get a week like this - not only defeats but the manner of the defeats - he knows himself more than anyone there's going to be a lot of scrutiny, criticism and introspection."

Lee: This is it for MON - his starting XI looked weak in midfield and proved to be. What he and the coaching staff have done to our big summer signings after bright starts is a worry. And the general fitness is telling, too.

Alec: What game was MON watching, to say it was a close game? Wow. It's quite obvious MON and coaches don't know best 11 or also a formation for them. How Ox can't get in that team and they can't see our midfield getting overrun every game is beyond me.

Kev: You can see O'Neill throwing the towel in here soon. I don't blame him. There's something smouldering at the club . This international break has come at the right time for Celtic. Dermot [Desmond] will be phoning his mate Pep for a hand at this rate.

Wayne: Let's be honest, getting beat is part of the game, as a fan you can accept that. What as fans you cannot accept is not giving it all, and that's the problem Celtic have at the moment, getting beat by average teams three games in a week. Shocking performances.

Danny: The board will keep O'Neill on as they think the fans won't turn but another loss today and it will become very toxic and all the good O'Neill has done will be forgotten.

articles.title: Simeone: "Por más que te llames Mourinho, Simeone o Flick no vale todo, no hay que pasar la línea del respeto"
articles.standfirst: El Cholo no está dispuesto a permitir que la 'rajada' del entrenador del Real Madrid empañe el triunfo del Atlético.
articles.summary: El Cholo no está dispuesto a permitir que la 'rajada' del entrenador del Real Madrid empañe el triunfo del Atlético.
articles.body: Simeone compareció tras el triunfo en el derbi. Rajada de Mourinho. "Somos respetuosos con lo que opinan los demás, estamos en lugar privilegiado en el que todos estamos muy expuestos, cualquier nombre, ya sea Simeone, Mourinho, Flick, Pellegrini... Necesitamos tener cuidado con lo que decimos y saber respetar a los demás. Perder, perdemos todos. Pero cuando uno sale de esa línea del respeto es peligroso, por más que te llames Mourinho, Flick o Simeone, no vale todo. No hay que pasar esa línea nunca". Jugadas polémicas. "Fue un partido intenso, ante un rival con unas transiciones increíble y las controlamos casi todas. En el segundo tiempo, sólo esa que se chocan Cuti y Llorente y deja a Diomande. Creo que controlamos en todo momento desde el trabajo colectivo, defensivo y grupal y sabiendo por dónde les podíamos hacer daño y no vamos a dejar de destacar el partido por esas cosas que quieren comentar. Cómo vio las expulsiones. "No opiné en las otras jugadas. El jefe de los árbitros ya nos dijo que este tipo de jugadas como la del Cuti no eran expulsión. Ahora si nos queremos detener en eso, pues vale, juguemos, Pero el partido lo ganamos". ¿Ganó el mejor? "Estás buscando un título y yo sinceramente no lo necesito. Hicimos un trabajo muy bueno colectivo, el equipo defendió muy bien ante grandes jugadores y los logramos contener. ¿Eso se vio o jugamos al juego que quieren que juguemos?. Triunfo. "Tengo claro lo que hizo el equipo, la alegría de nuestra gente una vez más después de que hace 15 años no era fácil y nos hace seguir creciendo como equipo. Es un paso más". Julián, redención. "Tenemos una gente increíble, no hay palabras de agradecimiento a todo lo que pudo atravesar de futbolista y de entrenador. Cuando entregas lo que tienes, te quieren. Julián lo intentó, le costó y lo vamos a recuperar. Y muy contento por Jonathan, nos da esa competencia para competir hasta donde podamos". Delante del Madrid al parón. "Nada importante ni determinante, es un punto positivo para el equipo, venimos creciendo y necesitamos seguir todos involucrados como Koke, suplente y juega el partido de su vida aunque su entrenador no lo ponga. Eso es el Atlético de Madrid. Necesitamos tratando de mejorar". Construcción. "Necesitamos el día a día, afrontar con la misma ilusión el Alavés, no salirnos del partido a partido y saber cuál es nuestra búsqueda y nuestro destino".

articles.title: Fulham v Man Utd player ratings: Matheus Cunha saves Man Utd with last minute equaliser
articles.summary: Last minute Cunha goal saves Man Utd from another defeat - who rated highest at Fulham?
articles.body:
Matheus Cunha's deflected last-minute equaliser spared Manchester United more misery after Lisandro Martinez's own goal had threatened to give Fulham victory at Craven Cottage.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Cunha rescues point for Man Utd at Fulham

Bernd Leno: On his toes to make an early save from Lisandro Martinez and scrambling when Matheus Cunha's effort looped on to a post. Denied Bryan Mbeumo with full-length save. 7

Timothy Castagne: Booked for bringing Marcus Rashford down as Manchester United broke in the second half. 6

David Affengruber: Excellent defence-splitting pass to release Josh King, but he couldn't finish. Exceptionally fortunate to escape after being outwitted by Cunha close to the goalline but stepped in to take the ball off Mbeumo as he looked to counter. 7

Calvin Bassey: Not the easiest game positionally as Manchester United played without an orthodox centre-forward. Got forward to create Fulham 's goal. 7

Antonee Robinson: Pushed into advanced areas in the inside forward position, which caused the visitors a defensive issue. 7

Sander Berge (Off, Larsson 76): Shot from the edge of the area turned away by Senne Lammens. 7

Shea Charles: Midfield partnership with Berge was key in protecting the Fulham defence when the visitors had extended spells of possession around the home area. Passing let him down on occasion. 6

Oscar Bobb (off Kevin, 70): Rolled an effort just wide of the post and probably should have done better. 6

Josh King (off Andersen, 79): Always looking to get on the ball and threaten. Took a good save from Lammens to deny him at the far post and his shot across goal was going in without the visitors' keeper kicking it away. Blotted his copybook by getting booked for diving. 8

Alex Iwobi (off Palacios, 70): Also tried to exploit the inside left channel when Fulham went forward. Low cross almost created a chance for Gonzalo Garcia and another deep one did for King. 7

Gonzalo Garcia (off Muniz, 79): Half a stride away from having a tap-in from an Iwobi cross from the left. 6

Palacios (on 70, Iwobi): Kept Fulham ticking over. 6

Subs not used: Lecomte, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon, Smith Rowe.

Senne Lammens: Key first-half saves to keep Manchester United level and came out bravely at Iwobi's feet to prevent another Fulham chance. Distribution could have been better and he didn't cover himself in glory with the Fulham goal. 6

Diogo Dalot: Tidy spin and dash into space to create a chance for Rashford but had too much work to do defensively as he lacked cover far too often. 6

Harry Maguire: Used his experience to draw a foul out of King as United tried to deal with Fulham pressure near their own goal. 7

Lisandro Martinez: Well-struck half-volley drew an excellent save out of Leno. He did eventually find the net - at the wrong end. 5

Luke Shaw (off Dorgu, 83): Returned from a three-match absence. Carrick's side are far more balanced when he is there. 7

Youri Tielemans: Wasted an excellent opportunity when he got no power behind his effort as he ran on to Rashford's short pass. 5

Kobbie Mainoo (off 79, Mount): Usual tidy game in possession without making the key passes. Never looks flustered. 7

Bryan Mbeumo: A lot of strong runs but, like many Man Utd forwards, nowhere near his best. Tough ask, but did he give Dalot enough defensive support? 6

Bruno Fernandes: Low shot against the post from Cunha cut-back but once more not at last season's levels. 6

Marcus Rashford (off 76, Zirkzee): Tried to set up Tielemans with a short pass but the Belgian couldn't finish. An attempt of his own before the break was saved by Leno and another, better opportunity flew way over the bar. 6

Matheus Cunha: Again started in the number nine role he doesn't seem suited to but created an excellent opportunity for Fernandes. Deflected shot hit the post and spun wide. Probably the visitors' most dangerous forward. 7

Subs not used: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Baleba, Lacey.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Al Fulham de Arbeloa se le escapa el triunfo en el 89' y sigue sin ganar
articles.standfirst: Los londinenses no pueden con el United y se quedan colistas con dos puntos en la tabla
articles.summary: Los londinenses no pueden con el United y se quedan colistas con dos puntos en la tabla
articles.body: El Fulham de Álvaro Arbeloa sigue sin ganar en la Premier League (vicecolista con dos puntos en cinco partidos) tras un choque en el que los londinenses estuvieron ganando hasta el minuto 89', en el que un gol de Matheus Cunha, tras un rebote desafortunado, dio al traste con el esfuerzo que estaba haciendo el once de Arbeloa, que se había adelantado con autogol de Lisandro Martínez en el 63'. Con Gonzalo García de titular, el Fulham sufrió mucho en algunos tramos del partido, con dos palos incluidos de Cunha (30') y Bruno (24') para el United, pero controlando luego bien el partido hasta el empate final (1-1). Curiosamente, los dos puntos del Fulham han sido contra Liverpool y United, amén de derrotas ante Chelsea, Palace y Sunderland. Tras el parón, jugarán de forma seguida ante Ipswich, Hull City y Coventry, los tres recién ascendidos. Una buenas oportunidad para cosechar los puntos que no tiene ahora. El partido se desarrolló con mucha tensión entre dos equipos que venían en crisis de puntos: uno para el Fulham y cuatro para un United que venía de dos derrotas seguidas (City en Premier y Brighton en Carabao). El Manchester United de Carrick estaba en una precrisis que solventa un poco con el empate en el 89'.

articles.title: Giuliano: "Respeto mucho a los árbitros porque primero son personas"
articles.standfirst: El argentino atendió a los medios tras el triunfo en el derbi
articles.summary: El argentino atendió a los medios tras el triunfo en el derbi
articles.body: Fue uno de los grandes protagonistas del choque ante el Madrid. Giuliano Simeone despachó un gran partido en el derbi forzando el penalti y asistiendo en el segundo gol rojiblanco. El pequeño de los Simeone atendió a los medios tras la victoria atlética. Cuestionan tu titularidad: "Siempre me miro a mí mismo, intento trabajar al máximo para el Atlético. Dedico las 24 horas del día para estar en la mejor forma posible para ayudar al equipo. Soy intenso en intentar mejorar, en mejorar técnicamente y en las virtudes que no tengo. Siempre con la humildad de estar con los pies en la tierra, nadie me va a regalar nada" El plus de ser Atlético: "Desde muy chiquito, ver al Atlético tantos partidos, tantos derbis importantes... es una forma en la que siento para jugar estos partidos. Es mi manera de ser o vivir, intento dar el máximo ante cualquier rival, vaciarme por completo como haría cualquier jugador o aficionado que tuviera esta ocasión" Rajada de Mourinho: "Tengo mucho respeto por los árbitros. Son personas, a veces aciertan y otras se equivocan. Si tomaron esa decisión lo vieron de esta manera. Respeto mucho a los árbitros porque primero son personas" Equipo: "Conocéis al entrenador. Va partido a partido. Son tres puntos importantes pero hay que mejorar como grupo. Seguir mejorando pero estamos contentos con la victoria" Poner el foco en que eres hijo de quién eres: "Yo también me pongo en lugar de la gente, mientras las críticas sean constructivas... sé que tengo mucho que mejorar técnicamente, mis movimientos, mi zurda, mi disparo desde fuera del área... para aportar al grupo cuando lo necesite y poder dar el 110%" Que el árbitro sea protagonista: "Siempre nos focalizamos en nosotros, no consumimos nada del exterior. Son noticias de ustedes. Trabajamos para mejorar como grupo"

articles.title: College Fantasy Football Week 4 Waiver Wire Pickups: Keelon Russell, Jamal Rule among players to add
articles.summary: College fantasy football analyst Eric Froton takes you through his top adds going into Week 4.
articles.body:
Week 3 had its share of theatrics and head-scratching finishes (looking at you, NC State ), along with several noteworthy college fantasy football performances to be aware of when mapping out your Week 4 waiver wire strategy. Here are the top performers from Week 3 who you should consider rostering.

The five-star freshman phenom was magnificent in a 50-36 revenge game victory over Florida State , completing 23-of-30 passes for 320 yards, three passing touchdowns to go with 56 rushing yards and another score on the ground. His 36.4 fantasy points were a career high and a marked improvement from the -9 rushing yards, two interceptions and 12.6 points he accrued last week against Kentucky. He had a few signature throws, but none more impressive than a laser he dropped over the shoulder of the defender for a 40-yard gain down the right sideline to WR Lotzeir Brooks.

Russell is settled in and brimming with confidence heading into a premium home matchup against a reeling South Carolina team that just blew a 16-0 lead to Mississippi State. The Bulldogs capitalized on two costly LaNorris Sellers interceptions to go on a 41-7 run and snuff out the shellshocked Gamecocks chances for victory. South Carolina HC Shane Beamer is feeling the heat from a fanbase that is starved for a contender after winning just one SEC game last year. That should translate into a very productive game for Russell, who is an automatic waiver add at his still sparse roster rate.

I told you to pick him up two weeks ago, now he's coming off a 45.9-point explosion against a quality Virginia defense. His dual-threat profile is combustible in four-point passing touchdown formats and he needs to be picked up everywhere ahead of a dream matchup against Oklahoma State.

Lincoln Kienholz , Louisville - 22% Rostered

Louisville is set to feast on the soft underbelly of its ACC schedule, and Kienholz is clearly the most capable signal-caller fantasy kingmakers Jeff and Brian Brohm have had under their tutelage since Tyler Shough.

I try to target players who are under 50% rostered, but the freshman sensation Rule simply cannot be left on any waiver wire going forward. His torrid start continued against North Dakota rushing 15 times for 119 yards and two touchdowns, including an explosive 55-yard, third-quarter scamper, for a sterling 29.4 fantasy points. That's only Rule's second-best fantasy game of the year after he charted a ridiculous 36.9 points in Week 1 versus Ohio. For perspective, only six running backs in the country averaged 20 fantasy PPG last year, while Rule is averaging 27.1 PPG through three games.

He projects as a quality starting option in Week 4, when the Cornhuskers travel to Michigan State, which just allowed 161 rushing yards in a 27-10 loss to Notre Dame, and allowed Toledo RB Connor Walendzak to rumble for 76 yards and a TD on just seven totes. New HC Pat Fitzgerald has assembled a respectable defensive front, but nothing that will keep Nebraska from giving Rule 15+ carries.

Keyjuan Brown , Louisville - 31% Rostered

One of the premium backup RBs during the preseason, Brown was a force down the stretch for the Cards last year, rushing for 94+ yards in each of his last five games while averaging 17.4 fantasy PPG over that span in relief of injured starter Isaac Brown. Keyjuan Brown's production was more modest the first two weeks of 2026. However, Isaac Brown was once again dinged up heading into their pivotal ACC showdown with SMU, leaving Keyjuan to turn 10 carries into 163 yards and two touchdowns, including a 58-yarder in which he burst through the line and displayed his trademark home-run ability.

Keyjuan is averaging a jaw-dropping 12.8 yards per carry thus far and has earned a more prominent role heading into Louisville's appealing early ACC stretch against Wake Forest, at NC State, vs. Florida State and at Syracuse.

How can you not love the energy from Kentucky and young gun HC Willie Stein following their 31-21 upset of Texas A&M. Baxter was instrumental in the win, logging 20 touches for 24.0 fantasy points and has a pair of likely victories over South Alabama and South Carolina on tap the next two weeks.

Nolan James Jr. , Notre Dame - 5% Rostered

It's official, the torch has been passed. Aneyas Williams has been supplanted by Nolan James Jr. as Notre Dame's RB1 following his showing against Michigan State, which included 26 carries for 121 yards, one TD and 19.8 fantasy points. He needs to be 100% rostered, pronto.

I realize his 39.4 half-PPR detonation comes with the "Bowling Green" caveat. But Flora is a clear RB1 in a favorable fantasy conference and has the pleasure of facing up-tempo West Virginia in two weeks, a team which allowed 425 total yards to Coastal Carolina earlier this season.

It's officially time to push Chris Durr Jr.'s roster rate above 50%, as the Terrapins' WR1 is in store for a breakthrough campaign. He is already averaging 12 targets, 96 yards and 24.8 fantasy points per game, and just exploded for an absurd 34.9 points against Virginia Tech this weekend. Keep in mind, Maryland has traditionally been one of the more pass-heavy P4 programs under HC Mike Locksley, and this season is no different as the Terps throw 84% of the time on passing downs (fifth in FBS) and 55% of the time on standard downs (11th).

Maryland's pass-heavy tendencies virtually ensure their WR1 is a fantasy-viable option. Durr has firmly established himself in that role, as his 12 receptions comprised 40% of UM's receptions versus the Hokies. Durr is a must-start in Week 4 against a feeble UCLA secondary that gave up 291 passing yards to Cal in Week 1, and just got ripped apart by Purdue QB Ryan Browne for 378 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air in a 52-38 bonanza.

Junior Sherrill , Vanderbilt - 22% Rostered

How quickly we forget Junior Sherrill was a vital component of former QB Diego Pavia's run to being a Heisman finalist last year. The third-year wideout caught 54-of-77 passes for 784 yards and seven touchdowns en route to a sparkling 2.8 fantasy points per touch with a 20% target share. Sherrill's impact last year was a bit understated due to the presence of departed TE Eli Stowers and WR Tre Richardson, but his 30.8% target share and 8.0 targets per game point to a sharp increase over his 2025 production.

Rocket-armed, five-star freshman QB Jared Curtis inevitably took over the starting quarterback job in Week 3, promptly connecting with WR1 Sherrill on 6-of-7 passes for 108 yards and two touchdowns. They have a fantasy-friendly showdown at Auburn, who play at the second-quickest pace in the nation and just let Florida hang 495 total yards and 44 points on them. Sherrill is a priority Week 4 waiver add for all WR-needy teams.

A classic example of my patented "POWR3 Theory" that emphasizes targeting wide receivers on teams capable of scoring 33+ points and throwing the ball 33+ times per game, Bowick is the run-away leader in routes run for the Cowboys with 109 so far this season. The next closest is WR Chris Barnes with 69, making Bowick's 34.3-point Week 3 eruption look sustainable.

Kenny Johnson , Texas Tech - 22% Rostered

When the chips were down and QB Will Hammond needed to make a play, he focused on Pitt transfer Kenny Johnson, who secured four of his eight targets with each reception going for 20+ yards. He leads all Red Raiders' wideouts in routes run, targets and receiving yards and should be viewed as Tech's WR1 going forward.

Micah Gilbert , Notre Dame - 0% Rostered

Gilbert was a revelation this week catching 8-of-9 targets for 170 yards for 21.0 fantasy points. Both Gilbert (63 routes) and veteran WR Jordan Faison (69) are the clear top-two wideouts in South Bend and the only ones worth rostering. Gilbert is worth a speculative streaming pickup against Purdue this weekend.

If there's anything we can bank on in college fantasy football, it's HC Sonny Dykes producing a noteworthy passing offense with multiple viable fatnasy options. Preseason projected WR1 Jordan Dwyer has yet to suit up, leaving room for slot WR Ed Small and TE Kari Ashley to establish themselves heading into their Week 4 tilt at UCF. Ashley has been unstoppable the last two weeks, recording 27.4 fantasy points in a 63-7 destruction of FCS Grambling, then reinforcing that breakout by reeling in all five of his targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in a more competitive 31-7 win over Arkansas State for 17.2 fantasy points. He currently ranks second among all P4 tight ends with 44.6 fantasy points on the year, behind only budding Virginia Tech superstar Luke Reynolds, who has already been featured multiple times in my columns. Adding Ashley is the highest priority for managers in search of a matchup-proof TE with upside.

Lofton was sparsely used in Miami's first two lopsided victories despite the Hurricanes amassing 854 passing yards. Yet, here he is securing 5-of-7 targets for 39 yards and a touchdown while looking particularly spry against Wake Forest.

articles.standfirst: Giuliano, MVP del partido, encarna la superioridad del Cholo sobre Mourinho en la pizarra y se erige en el futbolista más determinante 'secando' al Madrid y siendo el más punzante arriba
articles.summary: Giuliano, MVP del partido, encarna la superioridad del Cholo sobre Mourinho en la pizarra y se erige en el futbolista más determinante 'secando' al Madrid y siendo el más punzante arriba
articles.body: Apenas dos semanas de que cierto sector muy identificado de la crítica pusiera en duda su titularidad apelando a su apellido, el hijo (aunque ya lo había hecho con una galopada en el 95' para firmar un gol de puro gen en Anoeta) no ha encontrado mejor momento que el derbi para ejecutar el plan del padre. Giuliano no sólo sería la punta de lanza de la estrategia diseñada por Simeone desde la pizarra, sino que acabaría agigantándose, trasladando al verde la pasión inherente al ADN familiar, para erigirse en el futbolista que destrozó el esquema de Mourinho, en el ataque, y en el que secó a cuantos madridistas trataron de entrar por su costado, en defensa. Un MVP de libro que hace ridículo cualquier debate. Tenía claro El Cholo por dónde hacer daño al Real Madrid. Así que en el flanco entre Huijsen y Cucurella acumuló a Kang-in, Pubill y Llorente acompañando a Giuliano. Una carga de juego por esa zona que acabaría teniendo efecto nada más comenzar la segunda parte, cuando el omnipresente menor de los Simeone ganó la espalda a ambos tras un excepcional envío de Hancko a su carrera, forzando al central a derribarlo en el área. Expulsado el nuevamente internacional, sería el lateral el que se quedaría solo sufriendo el calvario. Así que apenas cinco minutos después, aprovechando un pase desde su misma banda de Kang in, Giuliano volvía a 'coger la moto' para dejar atrás a Cucurella y servir un preciso centro a Jonathan David, que sólo tuvo que empujar ante Courtois. Otra galopada plena de potencia, coraje y corazón. Sin embargo, el recital del hijo de Simeone no tendría una única dirección. Para cuando participó crucialmente en los dos goles del Atlético, Giuliano ya se había encargado de secar a Vinicius, incapaz de superarle una sola vez cuando se incrustaba de quinto defensa. Pero no sería el único al que desquiciaría con su intensidad, sacando también la peor versión de Bellinghan o de un Mbappe ante el que protagonizaría la mejor acción defensiva del partido, en pleno área y cuando el francés ya se disponía a rematar. Lo que no contaba es que hasta allí también llegara la pierna y el cuerpo del pequeño de los Simeone. Infranqueable, enorme, jugando como el hincha que da la vida por su equipo.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 4 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Ole Miss now occupies a top-five spot in the Associated Press Top 25 for the third straight season.
articles.body:
Ole Miss now occupies a top-five spot in the Associated Press Top 25 for the third straight season.

The Rebels moved up from eighth to fourth thanks to their dramatic 32-24 win over LSU on Saturday night. The Tigers, meanwhile, lost some ground, going from seventh to 10th.

Falling victim to the biggest upset in Week 3, Texas A&M tumbled a long way from its No. 9 position. The Aggies are in 23rd after losing 31-21 to Kentucky.

Top CFB winners and losers after dramatic slate

LSU vs. Ole Miss was one of the most anticipated games of 2026 with Lane Kiffin returning to Oxford.

The contest didn't disappoint as the Rebels jumped out to a 24-7 halftime lead before the Tigers tied the game in the fourth quarter. A 14-yard touchdown run by quarterback Trinidad Chambliss put Ole Miss back on top before LSU's Sam Leavitt threw an interception on 4th-and-goal from the 6-yard line to seal the outcome.

Chambliss threw for 363 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in a performance that could have Heisman Trophy implications. With the massive win, the Rebels burnished their credentials as a team with College Football Playoff ambitions.

By making the game close, LSU ensured its stock wouldn't take too much of a hit.

Texas A&M, on the other hand, knew what was coming after it laid an egg at home against Kentucky.

The Aggies trailed by 21 at one point before a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter at least made the final margin a little more flattering.

Coach Mike Elko will be disappointed by how little his defense disrupted the Wildcats. Kentucky quarterback Kenny Minchey was an efficient 14-of-18 for 252 yards and two touchdowns, while CJ Baxter and Jason Patterson combined to run for 145 yards.

A&M quarterback Marcel Reed also generated more concerns over whether he can be QB1 for a program with the Aggies' kind of expectations. He finished 26-of-49 for 236 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

A&M still has to play Missouri, Alabama, Tennessee, Oklahoma and Texas during the regular season. Maybe Saturday was a needed wakeup call. Otherwise, you can find two more losses on the Aggies' slate, and that would likely knock them out of the CFP hunt.

One of the most consequential games in Week 3 took place Friday night in Lubbock, Texas.

Houston quarterback Conner Weigman was inches away from breaking the plane and punching it in on his team's two-point conversion attempt.

Having edged past the Cougars, Texas Tech has a pretty straightforward path to the conference championship. The Red Raiders don't play another ranked opponent as they avoid BYU and Utah in Big 12 play.

Sure, you'd feel better about Tech with Brendan Sorsby at quarterback instead of Will Hammond. The rest of the roster appears to be good enough to mount another CFP challenge.

articles.title: Trinidad Chambliss Posts Epic Photo from Ole Miss Locker Room After Win vs. Lane Kiffin, LSU
articles.summary: Trinidad Chambliss wants everyone to know that Ole Miss is "just different."
articles.body:
Trinidad Chambliss wants everyone to know that Ole Miss is "just different."

The Ole Miss quarterback led the Rebels to a memorable 32-24 victory over former head coach Lane Kiffin and LSU on Saturday and then posted an epic picture celebrating with some of his teammates in the aftermath:

Top CFB winners and losers after dramatic slate

Chambliss certainly earned the right to celebrate.

He went 33-of-48 passing for 363 yards, two touchdowns and one interception while adding a score on the ground in the most important man. After LSU overcame a 24-7 halftime deficit to tie the game at 24 in the fourth quarter, Chambliss finished a 13-play, 75-yard drive with a 14-yard touchdown run that proved to be the difference.

Ole Miss then intercepted Sam Leavitt on LSU's ensuing possession, setting off the celebration for the Rebels and their fans.

The main storyline coming into the contest was Kiffin returning to Ole Miss to face his old team, but Chambliss' decision to stay with the Rebels instead of following his former head coach to join the Tigers proved large.

As a result, Ole Miss now has a marquee win on its early resume that will be quite important during the College Football Playoff race.

And if Chambliss continues to play at such a high level, he could be in Heisman discussions by the end of the season as well.

articles.title: Liverpool's Florian Wirtz put in one of his worst performances at Bournemouth and shouldn't play against Man City says Jamie Carragher
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz put in a poor first-half performance against Bournemouth, where Jamie Carragher said: "It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all"; Liverpool play Man City, Arsenal, Brentford and Brighton after the international break and Carragher says Wirtz should not be playing
articles.body:
Carragher criticised Wirtz during the first half of Liverpool's 1-0 win at the Vitality Stadium where he was on Sky Sports co-commentary duty. "Wirtz has been really poor again," he said. "It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all."

And after the game, the Sky Sports pundit claimed Wirtz will never reach the level that many people expected him to achieve at Anfield.

"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast made by Sky Sports .

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

"But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.

"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you. It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't."

'Iraola has decision to make - he can't be in the Man City team'

Liverpool face a crucial run of games straight after the lengthy, three-week international break. They return to a bumper fixture as Enzo Maresca's Manchester City visit Anfield on October 11, live on Sky Sports.

Andoni Iraola's side also face high-flying Brentford and Brighton in the Premier League, before hosting reigning champions Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on October 1.

In between all those games, Liverpool have Champions League tests with LASK and Villarreal, as well as a Carabao Cup fourth-round game against Chelsea.

Carragher feels Wirtz should not be in the Liverpool team to face City in that first fixture.

"I think going forward Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team," said Carragher.

"I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn't produce [against Bournemouth], he's then going to have a three-week break. By the time we come back, we're into October. Before you know it, it'll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it'll feel like we're getting to Christmas. He has to do something!

"If you go through the Premier League and think of players in his position - not just for the top teams, forget the top teams who we should be judging him against, I'm talking about normal Premier League players in the middle of the table - who have done more for their clubs.

"I think of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall at Everton. No one out there would say Dewsbury-Hall is a better player than Wirtz, or would go for more money than Wirtz, or would cost £120m. But every three or four weeks he scores a goal.

"I watched Morgan Gibbs-White for Nottingham Forest last week at Aston Villa, and in the second half he put in a performance in 45 minutes that Florian Wirtz has never done before for Liverpool.

"I've seen a goal Emiliano Buendia scored for Aston Villa at Tottenham. Again, these players aren't going to get over £100m, or £120m, but they're still giving their clubs bits every few weeks.

"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team.

"The things I've liked so far about Iraola, he's had the courage to make big decisions. Ryan Gravenberch has just signed a hefty contract on a five-year deal on massive money, because they thought him and Szoboszlai were going to be the future of the midfield going forward. He's not playing.

"Now, I can imagine the guys at the top of the club looking at that, thinking we've just given him a hefty contract. But no, he's not playing.

"The full-back situation, he keeps changing the full-backs, he's dropped Jeremie Frimpong straight away. Milos Kerkez has been in and out. So he's made decisions.

"But sooner or later he's going to have to make a decision on Florian Wirtz, and, for me, I hope it's sooner. Not because I don't like Florian Wirtz, I'm desperate for the kid to do well. I just want Liverpool to win. That's it, basically.

'Klopp is Liverpool's one hope regarding Wirtz'

However, Carragher feels Wirtz could be saved by former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp during the international break.

Klopp has selected Wirtz for Germany's upcoming Nations League games. Wirtz has been named in one of two separate Germany squads chosen by Klopp and the Liverpool midfielder will get a rest before being in contention to feature in Die Mannschaft's last two games against Serbia and Greece.

"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," said Carragher.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany, that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world, we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game, he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.

"I would love that to happen, I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."

articles.title: Mourinho busca burladero
articles.standfirst: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: El Barça vuela con Rodri, el Atlético rueda con Simeone y el Madrid se atasca con Mourinho. Así son las cosas tras la séptima jornada, cuando llega un corte que remite el retorno de LaLiga hasta el 10 de octubre. Tres semanas para rumiar los seis puntos de ventaja que ya le ha tomado el Barça al Madrid, derrotado ayer con merecimiento en el Metropolitano. El Atlético tiene juego, el Madrid tiene jugadores sin ensamblar. Los de arriba no bajan, los de atrás no elaboran. Eso no mezcla, es como agua y aceite. Se suponía que Mourinho tendría un plan para un Madrid sin Rodri, jugador cuya presencia en el equipo empezó a tener sentido desde el momento en que se trajo al entrenador portugués, pero no se ve. El Atlético se llevó un partido muy bronco en la primera parte, con el árbitro a merced de unas olas que él mismo levantó con sus primeros errores, pero en la segunda, con los ánimos serenados, se le vio superior. Y hay que destacar a Giuliano, sospechoso habitual, también para mí en los días malos, que no son muchos. Jugó muy bien por su lado (por cierto, desde que llegó al Madrid Cucurella está haciendo los peores partidos de su carrera), provocó el penalti con expulsión de Huijsen que valió el 0-1, le dio a Jonathan David el 2-0 y le quitó de la punta de la bota a Mbappé lo que pudo ser el 2-2 final, reaccionando magníficamente a una maniobra mágica del francés. El Atlético se llevó, además de la satisfacción de ganar un derbi con todos sus avíos (llenazo, dureza, nervios, tarde reventona, arbitraje polémico…) y los tres puntos, la reconciliación con Julián Alvarez casi lograda. El Cholo le sacó sabiamente a partido ganado, el delantero jugó con interés y volvieron los aplausos. Mourinho se parapetó en el arbitraje. Con menos estrépito que en otro tiempo, un poco tirando la piedra y escondiendo la mano, se metió en ese burladero. Bueno para sus incondicionales, que son menos que en su primera época, pero quedan, y al fin y al cabo se alinea así con la doctrina que en su ausencia ha mantenido RMTV con el respaldo, hay que decirlo, del conocimiento en estos años de su ausencia del bochornoso negreirato que, aunque cosa ya pasada, aún es un pozo del que sacar agua porque sigue abierto. Al menos el Madrid puede rescatar una cosa de este partido: la convicción de que Diomande hace, a día de hoy, más que Vinicius en la banda izquierda. Mourinho se atrevió a quitar al brasileño en el 53’ y a partir de ese momento sí hubo peligro por ese costado. Lástima que también quitó a Güler en lugar de a Bellingham para dar entrada a un central. Pero si al menos Mourinho le ha perdido el respeto reverencial a Vinicius, hay algo bueno a lo que agarrarse. Parecía que el Barça lo tenía todo menos un ‘9’, y he aquí que un clásico extremo se ha adaptado a la posición a las mil maravillas. Llegados aquí, ya no parece que se trate de una buena racha, porque son 9 goles en 6 jornadas de campeonato. El parche va para pichichi, quién sabe si para Bota de Oro. Le favorece, como a todos sus compañeros, algo a lo que él mismo, como todos los demás, contribuye: el buen juego colectivo. O sea, la mano de Flick. Cuando un equipo funciona, todos sus integrantes lucen, en cualquier zona del campo. Del Real Unión me hablaba con respeto mi padre, pues fue tres veces campeón de Copa y por ello estuvo entre los fundadores de la Liga. Poco antes de la primera edición estrenó campo, ese Stadium Gal que acaba de celebrar 100años. Su fachada da a la calle Patricio Arabolaza, que evoca al autor del primer gol en la historia de la selección, un jugador corajudo que corregía sus pies planos con unas artesanales suelas de corcho. En el Real Unión, ahora en la Primera RFEF, aún resuenan los ecos de un tiempo heroico.

articles.title: Parte médico de Valverde: traumatismo severo en el tobillo izquierdo
articles.standfirst: El jugador acabó lesionado tras la entrada de Kang In Lee y mañana pasará más pruebas
articles.summary: El jugador acabó lesionado tras la entrada de Kang In Lee y mañana pasará más pruebas
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha emitido un parte médico sobre el estado físico de Fede Valverde, que acabó lesionado del tobillo izquierdo tras la dura entrada de Kang In Lee. "Tras las pruebas realizadas hoy a nuestro jugador Fede Valverde por los Servicios Médicos del Real Madrid se le ha diagnosticado un traumatismo severo en el tobillo izquierdo, sufrido en el encuentro de esta tarde. Valverde será sometido a nuevas pruebas en las próximas horas", reza el comunicado médico del Real Madrid La entrada del coreano sobre Valverde fue la que más indignó al Real Madrid y a Jose Mourinho, por encima de la del Cuti Romero a Jude Bellingham. Desde el club blanco no se entiende cómo ni el colegiado sobre el césped ni el VAR vieron una acción que no admite discusión viéndola por la televisión. Fede pudo acabar el partido, pero mañana será sometido a más pruebas médicas y peligra su presencia con la selección.

articles.title: La conexión canaria tumba al Levante e ilumina La Cerámica
articles.standfirst: Ayoze abrió el camino, Moleiro -tras una genialidad de Akhomach- sentenció y Mikautadze puso la guinda al triunfo amarillo ante un conjunto granota que nunca se rindió
articles.summary: Ayoze abrió el camino, Moleiro -tras una genialidad de Akhomach- sentenció y Mikautadze puso la guinda al triunfo amarillo ante un conjunto granota que nunca se rindió
articles.body: La luz llegó desde las islas en una noche encendida en La Cerámica. Ayoze Pérez y Alberto Moleiro activaron la conexión canaria para derribar a un Levante indomable, de esos que se levantan cada vez que parecen vencidos. El primero abrió una puerta que Iván Romero se empeñó en cerrar y el segundo, impulsado por una genialidad de Akhomach, terminó guiando al Villarreal hacia un triunfo tan trabajado como luminoso donde Mikautadze puso la guinda. Los amarillos llevaron el peso de una primera parte que fue inclinando poco a poco hacia la portería de Ryan. Ilias Akhomach agitó el ataque amarillo desde la derecha y Ayoze rozó el gol a los tres minutos, pero Toljan salvó su remate sobre la línea. El Submarino arrancó volcánico. El Levante resistió bien aseadito y buscó sorprender al contragolpe, como en una ocasión de Thiago que terminó en el lateral de la red. El plan parecía claro por cada orilla. Los de Íñigo, con ganas de sacudirse definitivamente la sosería, intensificaron su dominio con el paso de los minutos, aunque les faltó precisión en el área. Moleiro desperdició una llegada clara y Ayoze volvió a encontrarse con la defensa granota cuando Brugué taponó su disparo. El equipo de Iñigo Pérez acumulaba posesión, territorio y ocasiones, mientras el Levante apenas conseguía inquietar a Gulacsi. La recompensa amarilla llegó en el minuto 41 con una preciosa combinación entre Moleiro y Ayoze, culminada por el delantero ante la salida de Ryan. Plas. Sin embargo, la alegría duró apenas un suspiro: en la siguiente acción, Toljan centró e Iván Romero firmó una espectacular volea acrobática para devolver el empate. Quizá el gol de la jornada. Dos fogonazos consecutivos mandaron el partido al descanso con un 1-1 tan vibrante como inesperado. El Villarreal regresó del descanso con el colmillo afilado y encontró premio en un error granota. Akhomach convirtió una pérdida en una genialidad: un tacón exquisito, de esos que iluminan una jugada, dejó solo a Moleiro ante Ryan. El canario no perdonó y devolvió al Submarino una ventaja que Buchanan pudo ampliar poco después, aunque su disparo acarició el poste. El gol obligó al Levante a soltarse las cadenas. El conjunto granota adelantó líneas, se instaló por momentos en campo rival y discutió el gobierno del partido a un Villarreal que perdió el control, pero encontró campo abierto para amenazar. Gerard Moreno rozó la sentencia y Toljan tuvo el empate en sus botas tras una mala salida de Gulacsi, aunque Renato Veiga apareció a tiempo para desviar el peligro. Cuando el Levante todavía soñaba con rescatar un punto, otro error en la salida terminó por apagar su rebelión. Gerard robó, Moleiro dibujó el pase y Mikautadze resolvió el mano a mano para poner el 3-1. La Cerámica respiró entonces tranquila: el Villarreal, sin excesivo brillo pero con una contundencia feroz, castigó cada concesión y convirtió los fallos granotas en el combustible de su victoria.

articles.title: El Almería resuelve en 18 minutos y va tomando posiciones
articles.standfirst: Tercera victoria seguida para ascender hasta el 4º puesto y el filial del Celta cierra una dura semana con dos derrotas y media docena de goles en contra
articles.summary: Tercera victoria seguida para ascender hasta el 4º puesto y el filial del Celta cierra una dura semana con dos derrotas y media docena de goles en contra
articles.body: El Almería volvió a demostrar fortaleza en casa para imponerse al Celta Fortuna. Los rojiblancos suman su tercera victoria consecutiva y tan sólo han perdido un encuentro en casa de los últimos 13 de Liga disputados en el UD Almería Stadium. En el minuto 2, Miguel de la Fuente la estrelló en el poste. Poco después, Embarba probó fortuna con un remate con poco ángulo que Coke Carrilo blocó con el pecho. Y a la tercera, el 1-0. Nico Melamed recibió de Javi Muñoz en la frontal del área y saca un disparo seco, ajustado a la cepa del poste, imposible para el portero. Sólo se habían disputado seis minutos. Capdevila estuvo a punto de firmar el gol del partido con un trallazo desde 40 metros que terminó repelido por el larguero. Pero los de García Pimienta sí aprovecharon su siguiente oportunidad. Marcos Luna puso un gran centro que remató Javi Muñoz al fondo de la red con un toque sutil. 2-0 en el 18'. Nico Melamed y Cipenga pudieron ampliar aún más la ventaja antes del descanso. La segunda mitad comenzó con cambios en ambos equipos. Miguel de la Fuente perdonó nada más reanudarse el juego al rematar prácticamente solo desde el punto de penalti, aunque su disparo se marchó desviado. En el 49', Óscar Marcos desaprovechó un mano a mano ante Andrés Fernández. El centrocampista del filial vigués volvió a intentarlo en el 81' con un buen disparo desde la frontal que se marchó fuera por muy poco. Tampoco fue el día de Miguel, que volvió a desperdiciar una ocasión clarísima con toda la portería para él tras una brillante triangulación entre Arribas, Morcillo y el propio delantero. El Almería va tomando posiciones: ya es 4º y encadena tres partidos con su portería imbatida.

articles.title: El Burgos se apunta a otra remontada: Córdoba, Ceuta y Las Palmas
articles.standfirst: Álex Forés neutralizó el tanto de Jesé en la primera mitad y David González lo sentenció con un gol en el 94'
articles.summary: Álex Forés neutralizó el tanto de Jesé en la primera mitad y David González lo sentenció con un gol en el 94'
articles.body: El fútbol premió a un Burgos valiente. Se llevó los tres puntos del Gran Canaria porque, cuando consiguió el empate, se lanzó a por la victoria. Lo hizo remontando un partido que se le puso cuesta arriba a los 37 minutos, tras un disparo seco y duro de Jesé, que diez minutos antes había avisado con otro misil que se estrelló en el larguero. Y es que los amarillos dominaron durante buena parte del encuentro, pero no supieron aprovechar su buena primera parte, ni sostener su ventaja tras el descanso. El paso por vestuarios le sentó bien al Burgos, que no había disfrutado apenas del balón en el primer acto. Aunque Las Palmas mantuvo la intención de ir a por el segundo con Iván Jaime y Jesé como principales argumentos ofensivos, el partido dio un giro inesperado. Los 'Hijos del frío' encontraron petróleo en una contra que comandó Forés. El delantero, que llevaba apenas 12 minutos en el césped, dejó atrás a Bonfanti y se plantó solo ante Caro para superar al portero con una vaselina. Herzog tuvo tiempo para despejar bajo palos, pero -inexplicablemente, dejó pasar el balón hasta tal punto que no pudo despejar cuando quiso reaccionar. El gol espoleó al Burgos, que comenzó a buscar una y otra vez la espalda de la defensa amarilla, generando superioridades. Y lo consiguió en el último suspiro del partido en, como no, otra contra a la espalda de los centrales amarillos. Esta vez fue David González el que se quedó solo delante de Caro para ganar el partido.

articles.title: Fulham 1-1 Man Utd: Matheus Cunha's deflected shot cancels out Lisandro Martinez horror own goal in draw at Craven Cottage
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Manchester United avoid defeat at Fulham thanks to Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike after a shocking own goal from Lisandro Martinez piled on the pressure; Fulham still searching for first Premier League win under Alvaro Arbeloa but move off bottom
articles.body:
A horror-show own goal from Lisandro Martinez with 23 minutes to play piled the pressure on United to snatch something from this match, following the midweek Carabao Cup collapse at home to Brighton and Manchester derby defeat last weekend.

A wicked flick off David Affengruber got them out of jail. But United are still in the bottom half of the Premier League after five games, 10 points adrift of table-topping neighbours City and looking miles off the level required to challenge the country's best sides this season. This is their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign.

"A real mess" was how Sky Sports' Gary Neville described the own goal. Cunha was levered off the ball by Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey, whose stinging shot was parried by Senne Lammens. The 'keeper then saw Martinez stick out a boot and divert the ball back past him. Lammens' clumsy attempt to cut it out summed up United's chaotic defending.

It was their play on the ball before that which most worried Neville, though. He called their passive possession before the opener "the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen Manchester United play".

The narrative could have been very different had Bruno Fernandes found the net rather than the post from Cunha's inviting cutback in the first half, or if the Brazilian's heavily deflected shot had gone in rather than clipped the woodwork. Bernd Leno also made a series of full-stretch saves.

Eventually, the Fulham 'keeper was beaten, with no chance of stopping the leveller. It was heartbreak for the hosts and their new boss Alvaro Arbeloa who is still searching for his first Premier League win. He will take encouragement from this performance after their draw at Anfield, though, as they move off bottom spot by goal difference.

As for United, the accumulation of poor performances already this season will have alarm bells ringing in Manchester. They got away with a point at Fulham but have to find a way to make a major gear change during the upcoming three-week break to get back on track and realise their ambitions of kicking on this season.

Cunha: They put in more energy than us - we cannot accept this

"It is so frustrating for us. In the beginning, we put the plan in and created some chances. We didn't score and then they scored in one action. It is hard to explain.

"It is frustrating for us. After the goal, we played much better and had a lot of character. It needs to be from the start. It is only one point but we should never play for one point.

"It is hard. They put in more energy than us, we cannot accept this. We need to do our best. We need to improve in every single position. It is only the beginning. Last season was the same, with noise around, but we finished third."

Carrick: We created enough to win the game

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to Sky Sports:

"I thought we should've won the game, we created enough to win the game. We had a lot of good play and the goal we did concede, it is one of those goals.

"I really liked the reaction and how we finished the game. It would be easy for it to go in another direction.

"We nearly won it at the end. We came to get the win; of course we did, but the way we finished the game is the positive we take from it.

"Their goalkeeper, the saves he has made, he was player of the match and we hit the post twice. A lot of it [our play] was good. There are things to take from it, for sure."

Fulham boss A lvaro Arbeloa to Sky Sports:

"We were so close. So, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

"Also we knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referees have been doing in all the matches so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.

"All fouls for them. You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, it's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here. We deserved a little bit more."

In his press conference, Arbeloa appeared to row back on his comments a little bit - but still said he "was not really happy".

"My English is not so good," he said. "Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.

"When you say something that you don't have to say, it's better to stay calm, focus on the performance of my team and focus on the next game.

"I'm not really happy. Like I said, I need to be focused and put my energy in all the things that I have to improve.

"[Maguire] is a very big guy and maybe it wasn't a foul. But it's ok. Like I said, I prefer to analyse the game - players, systems and it's the best for win.

"You know when you draw a game like that, maybe you're a little bit frustrated."

10: SAVE! Martinez flies a shot from just outside the Fulham box towards the top-corner after a half-cleared cross - but Leno stretches to push it away.

25: POST! Cunha gets around Affengruber and cuts the ball back but Fernandes steers his shot against the far post.

28: SAVE! Lammens saves Josh King's volley from close quarters when the youngster meets Alex Iwobi's cross.

31: CHANCES! Gonzalo Garcia miscues a volley and Sander Berge has his follow-up shot well saved by Lammens before Oscar Bobb drags wide from another good position for Fulham.

31: POST! A big deflection loops Cunha's shot over Leno and against the far post, with the ball coming back off the 'keeper and out for a corner.

32: SAVE! Lammens is forced into another good stop, sticking out a leg to keep out King's strike.

63: OWN GOAL! After a sleepy start to the second half, Bassey overpowers Cunha and fires a shot which Lammens parries - and is bundled back past him by Martinez

67: SAVE! Leno stretches to save Bryan Mbeumo's curling shot.

74: SAVE! Leno again at full stretch to deny Cunha.

86: PENALTY APPEALS! Man Utd want a penalty for handball from Bassey after Martinez turns the ball against him. But his arms are tucked into his body.

89: GOAL! Cunha's deflected shot grabs United a last-gasp equaliser.

articles.title: Villares castiga el conservadurismo del Betis en Riazor
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos se dejaron ir en la segunda parte y el Deportivo araña un empate en el 86'
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos se dejaron ir en la segunda parte y el Deportivo araña un empate en el 86'
articles.body: El Betis no ha podido continuar con su racha victoriosa. En su tercer partido en siete días, el equipo de Pellegrini ha pagado su conservadurismo en la segunda parte frente al Deportivo de La Coruña y ha visto cómo en un partido que tenía prácticamente ganado, se le han escapado dos puntos a cuatro minutos del 90. Marcó Cucho en la primera parte, pudieron sentenciar los verdiblancos, pero el conjunto gallego no le perdió la cara al choque y terminó encontrando con un testarazo de Villares el merecido premio a la insistencia. Los andaluces, que venían de tres triunfos seguidos en LaLiga, desaprovechan la oportunidad de irse al parón en la segunda plaza de la clasificación. Con 16 puntos, se mantendrán en el tercer puesto antes de recuperar fuerzas tras unos días altísima exigencia con la competición doméstica y el estreno en la Champions. Los gallegos alcanzan ya los 10 puntos en las siete primeras fechas y evitan sufrir su segunda derrota consecutiva en casa en apenas cuatro días. Con un Betis recuperando su once más 'titular', a falta únicamente de Isco, y un Deportivo castigado por un virus, sin Aubameyang, entre otros, el comienzo del partido fue el esperado. Los de Pellegrini dominaban y llegaban con cierta facilidad a las inmediaciones del área gallega. Estuvieron cerca de marcar antes de los cinco minutos en una falta lateral lanzada por Fornals al segundo palo que Roca devolvió a la zona de peligro para que Bartra probara suerte de chilena. Leo Román, con una manopla espectacular, le negó el gol al central catalán. La suerte le volvió a ser esquiva a Marc, esta vez en forma de lesión. En una acción defensiva en la que pareció cometer falta sobre Bil Nsongo, no señalada, el capitán bético se hizo daño en un muslo y tuvo que ser sustituid por Valentín Gómez. A partir de ahí, el partido fue perdiendo fuelle. A los de verdiblancos, hoy de verde y dorado, les faltaba precisión en sus llegadas por las dos bandas. Los blanquiazules lo que echaban de menos era calidad en las pocas veces que lograban llegar arriba. Poco después de la media hora, el Deportivo perdió uno de sus faros en el centro del campo. Casadó cayó mal sobre el césped en una acción en la que Fornals le chocó intentando robar un balón y se hizo daño en un hombro. Otro cambio antes del descanso, esta vez preocupante porque el exjugador del Barcelona se fue al banquillo con gestos de dolor y diciendo "se me ha roto, se me ha roto". Demasiados contratiempos en un partido en el que no estaba pasando casi nada. Mella, con un golpeo flojito desde la frontal, no pudo sorprender a Valles en una acción que partió de un claro codazo de Navarro a Fran García, no señalado. Y cuando parecía que se llegaría al descanso sin pena ni gloria, el partido se rompió. Giménez ganó un balón dividido a Fornals en el área, pero su equipo no fue capaz de alejarlo. Deossa lo peleó y terminó llevándoselo, se lo dio al Cucho y el colombiano, desde la frontal, sacó un latigazo seco, raso, pegado al palo, para poner el 0-1 en el marcador. Los de Antonio Hidalgo trataron de reaccionar, pero se llegó al intermedio con una polémica que paró el partido algunos minutos. El Cucho quiso prolongar de tacón en el aire una jugada en el centro del campo, llegó primero y tocó claramente el balón. Pero en su gesto de querer impulsar el esférico, impactó con su bota en la cabeza de Navarro, que estaba en todas. López Toca desde el VAR llamó a Soto Grado para que viera la jugada en el monitor. El riojano mantuvo su decisión y se armó la marimorena, con un Riazor encendido. Lo cierto es que el Cucho en ningún momento ve llegar a Navarro, que va tarde y mete la cabeza. Pero por la altura de la acción pudo haberse considerado perfectamente como temeraria y haberle costado una amarilla que tampoco vio, más aún al impactar en la cabeza del defensa. Lo cierto es que el árbitro no consideró que la jugada fuera merecedora de tarjeta alguna y el partido se fue al descanso en medio de una bronca monumental cuando los jugadores, y en especial Soto Grado, enfilaba el camino hacia los vestuarios. El enfado de la afición deportivista continuó en el regreso al césped de los protagonistas y pareció darle cierto impulso a su equipo, que salió con ganas de mostrar otra imagen. Asp Jensen, con un golpeo que bloqueó la defensa, fue el primero en intentarlo. También probó suerte el Deportivo a balón parado en una acción de estrategia desde la esquina que culminó Giménez de cabeza. Al igual que a otro intento posterior del danés, lo paró Valles, cuyo gran comienzo de temporada no ha sido suficiente para convencer a De la Fuente tras la lesión de Joan García. Para entonces, el conjunto gallego ya era dominador total del partido y del balón. A Pellegrini no le gustaba un pelo lo que estaba viendo y preparaba cambios. Pero antes de que pudiera llevarlos a cabo, Soriano filtró un pase fantástico a la espalda de Fran García para que Mella se quedara completamente solo delante de Valles. El guardameta de La Rinconada, de nuevo salvador, evitó el empate en el mano a mano. Una parada valor gol antes de que Isco y Facundo entraran al campo. El plan del Ingeniero era claramente defenderse con balón y forzar al Dépor a adelantar líneas para buscar después los espacios. Así llegó una doble ocasión clarísima. Balón largo a Abde que controla de maravilla, se plante ante Leo Román y remata muy escorado, casi sin ángulo para encontrar portería. Pero el rechace fue a las botas del Cucho que, esta vez, pecó de egoísmo. Tenía completamente solo a Isco para marcar, pero lo intentó él y se encontró con las piernas de los defensas. Hidalgo aceptó el envite del Betis y, ya que ahora le iba a costar tener más el valón, buscó la velocidad de Aubameyang, que no tardó en generar problemas con un remate que se fue a córner. Con espacios y un Abde imparable, el Betis estuvo cerca del 0-2. El marroquí provocó un córner que remató Natan de cabeza al travesaño. La respuesta del Deportivo, un centro lateral desde la izquierda que remató 'Auba' intentando pillar a Valles a contrapié. Imposible, las para todas. Incluso cuando los rivales estaban fuera de juego, como Yeremay recién ingresado al césped, aparecía Álvaro para echar el candado a su portería. Pero tanto tentar la suerte fue demasiado incluso para el portero más en forma de LaLiga. Un buen centro desde la izquierda de Soriano lo cabeceó a la red Villares llegando desde atrás para premiar el esfuerzo del Dépor en la segunda parte y castigar el conservadurismo de un Betis que, sin embargo, pudo hacer el 1-2 casi a continuación en una jugada que Riquelme desaprovechó de manera incomprensible.

articles.title: El Brujas de Virgili da un golpe sobre la mesa
articles.standfirst: Golea al Genk (3-0) y se mantiene a un punto de un Unión SG que se impuso al Amberes (0-2)
articles.summary: Golea al Genk (3-0) y se mantiene a un punto de un Unión SG que se impuso al Amberes (0-2)
articles.body: Era un día importante para el Brujas en su objetivo por revalidar el título de la Jupiler Pro League reconquistado la temporada pasada. Recibían al Genk en el Jan Breydel Stadium y dieron un golpe encima de la mesa (3-0). Virgili, convocado por David Gordo con la Sub21 de cara a este parón de selecciones, volvió a arrancar como titular en la banda izquierda del Brujas por tercer partido consecutivo por delante de un Diakhon a quien Patrick Vieira ha citado con Senegal en su debut como seleccionador. Fue Carlos Forbs, sin embargo, quién comenzó a 'destrozar' el partido justo cuando se cumplía el primer cuarto de hora. Recibió de Vanaken, giró a una velocidad supersónica y le buscó las cosquillas a Brughmans -fichado por el Liverpool por más de 30 millones- con un disparo ajustado al palo corto. Quinto gol generado por el extremo luso este curso. Ya en la segunda parte, el VAR entró en acción para anular el tanto de un Nicoló Tresoldi que, de momento, sigue yendo con la Sub21 de Alemania. Pero, en cuestión de cinco minutos, Seys sacó a relucir su guante para regalarle dos asistencias a Han-Beom Lee y Mechele que dejaron el partido resuelto. Brughmans, eso sí, evitó un castigo todavía mayor para un Genk tremendamente irregular en este inicio de curso. El Brujas, a pesar del triunfo, ya sabía desde antes del partido que no podía asaltar el liderato antes de marcharse anterior. Se mantiene por detrás del Gent, que se impuso el viernes al Standard Lieja, y un Unión SG que venció al Amberes a domicilio (0-2) con los goles de Biondic y Roeve en la segunda parte.

articles.title: Alvaro Arbeloa accuses officials of not wanting Manchester United to lose after late controversy in draw at Fulham
articles.summary: Man Utd rescued a late 1-1 draw at Fulham after Matheus Cunha's deflected equaliser; Alvaro Arbeloa felt Harry Maguire winning a free-kick 35 seconds before the equaliser for a 'foul' by Cesar Palacios was soft; Arbeloa felt the refs were kinder to United after the Manchester derby drama
articles.body:
United rescued a 1-1 draw after Matheus Cunha scored a deflected 89th-minute equaliser - but Fulham head coach Arbeloa was furious that, 35 seconds before the goal, United were given a free-kick for a foul on Harry Maguire on the halfway line.

Arbeloa felt the free-kick for Cesar Palacios' foul on Maguire was soft and claimed referee Michael Oliver and his team of officials gave "all fouls" to United - because of the "error in judgement" by the officials who incorrectly awarded Erling Haaland's Manchester derby winner at Old Trafford last weekend.

"All fouls for them," Arbeloa told Sky Sports. "You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, he's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them.

"And I knew. I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here. We deserved a little bit more.

"We were so close. So, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

"Also we knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referees have been doing all the match so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky."

In his press conference, Arbeloa appeared to row back on his comments a little bit - but still said he "was not really happy".

"My English is not so good," he said. "Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.

"When you say something that you don't have to say, it's better to stay calm, focus on the performance of my team and focus on the next game.

"I'm not really happy. Like I said, I need to be focused and put my energy in all the things that I have to improve.

"[Maguire] is a very big guy and maybe it wasn't a foul. But it's ok. Like I said, I prefer to analyse the game - players, systems and it's the best for win.

"You know when you draw a game like that, maybe you're a little bit frustrated."

Is it a foul? Young and Saha analyse the decision

Analysing the Maguire foul on Super Sunday, former Manchester United defender Ashley Young told Sky Sports: "It's definitely a foul. Palacios isn't looking at the ball, he's straight into Maguire's back.

"I know he [Arbeola] says Maguire is 100kg, but he's smart, he's waiting for the foul to be committed."

Asked if it was a foul, former Fulham and Manchester United forward Louis Saha added: "It is.

"It might be soft, but that's where some players have experience, they use their body in the right way. In his position, he [Maguire] felt like he couldn't take the control so it was a clever piece of work from Maguire."

Should Man Utd have been given penalty for Bassey handball?

Another talking point came just before United's equaliser - when Fulham defender Calvin Bassey was accused of handball after Lisandro Martinez's ball forward into the penalty area.

VAR looked at the decision but agreed with the assistant referee's view that Bassey had his arm close to his body - even though it struck his hand.

"He did put his hand up," said Gary Neville on co-commentary. "The fact that the hand is close to the body might save him."

Analysing the decision, Saha said: "Its kind of a 50:50, you don't know now with the rules. It hits his hand. The natural instinct you have is to protect your face because you know you're going to be hit.

"It's different rules every weekend, we don't understand it. Some will blow, some will go on."

articles.title: CFP Playoff Bracket, Scenarios and Bowl Projections After 2026-27 Week 4 AP Rankings
articles.summary: The SEC possesses three of the top four spots in the AP Top 25.
articles.body:
The SEC possesses three of the top four spots in the AP Top 25.

The Ole Miss Rebels' four-spot jump into the No. 4 spot of the Week 4 Top 25 gave the SEC the early advantage over the Big Ten in the fight to be the conference in college football in 2026. A total of 10 SEC teams are ranked going into Week 4.

Ole Miss and the top-ranked Texas Longhorns have the two best wins of the early season.

Ole Miss took down the LSU Tigers in a top-10 showdown on Saturday night, while Texas defeated the Ohio State Buckeyes last week.

The balance of power will continue to trade hands throughout the regular season, but for now, the top is controlled by the SEC.

Ole Miss Joins Texas, Georgia as SEC Teams In Top 4

Ole Miss was the most notable mover in Sunday's AP poll.

The Rebels' jump from No. 8 to No. 4 reflected the difficulty of their win over LSU.

At the moment, Ole Miss is in the top four alongside fellow SEC programs Texas and Georgia. The Rebels play both of the top two teams later in the season.

In fact, Ole Miss can't rest on its win over LSU being enough to qualify for the College Football Playoff.

Week 4's road trip to Florida is now more difficult given the Gators' fast start under Jon Sumrall and new position inside the Top 25.

Ole Miss now has four Top 25 opponents left on its schedule. The goal would be to at least go 2-2 in those games to reach 10-2 and an at-large berth into the playoff.

However, it's easy to have larger expectations for Trinidad Chambliss and Co. after they beat LSU.

Chambliss is arguably the best quarterback in the country and he proved once again that he could solve a tough defense throughout the win over LSU.

Texas and Georgia might be higher up on the list of national title contenders right now, but Ole Miss is certainly in a position to move up that hierarchy as the season goes on.

LSU and Texas A&M all of a sudden find themselves involved in a potential playoff elimination game in Week 4.

LSU fell three spots to No. 10 on Sunday, while Texas A&M tumbled 14 spots to No. 23 following its home loss to Kentucky.

The loser of Saturday night's clash in Baton Rouge will have two defeats before October and with just two SEC games under its belt.

LSU appears to be in better shape because it plays at home in Week 4, but even if it beats A&M, it's not out of the clear with Alabama, Texas and Tennessee on the schedule in November.

A&M still has Missouri, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee on its schedule after LSU, so there's a chance that a loss in Baton Rouge sends the Aggies on a spiral out of the Top 25 and far away from the playoff conversation.

The SEC is loaded at the top, so there will be plenty of movement in the standings, but it'll be difficult to make a case for either LSU or A&M to go perfect in October and November after suffering two losses early.

Louisville Has Sights Set On Playoff With Seven-Spot Jump

The Louisville Cardinals vaulted seven spots up to No. 16 after its win over the SMU Mustangs.

Louisville appears to be in an ideal spot to be the ACC's second team into the playoff behind the Miami Hurricanes.

Jeff Brohm's team has no ranked opponents left on its schedule. It is 1-1 against Top 25 teams already with a win over SMU and a loss to Ole Miss.

The SEC and Big Ten teams ahead of Louisville will continue to beat each other week-by-week, which should allow the Cardinals to inch up into the top 10 by the end of October if they keep winning.

There's still plenty of games left to play, but if you're Louisville, you must be ecstatic about the position you are through three weeks with that remaining schedule.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho: Real Madrid boss holds up pictures of referee errors in press conference after defeat to Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho held up pictures of refereeing errors following 2-1 defeat to Atletico Madrid; Mourinho claimed referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias couldn't "cope with the pressure"; he claimed Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in should have both been sent off
articles.body:
Mourinho strongly criticised the officials and was angry that Atletico defender Cristian Romero ‌ was not sent off for a stamp on Jude Bellingham .

He also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde , before the visitors were reduced to 10 men five minutes after half-time.

"We could skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," ​Mourinho said, holding up the images in what was the start of a near ‌five-minute rant.

"Those were two clear red cards. The difficulties we've faced since the sending-off - 11 against 10 - well, we can imagine what 50 ​minutes of 11 against nine would have been like if justice had been done."

Real defender Dean Huijsen was dismissed for bringing down Giuliano Simeone inside the area as the last defender, allowing Alejandro Grimaldo to ​score with a low spot-kick.

Jonathan David doubled Atletico's lead six minutes later, ⁠with Antonio Rudiger heading in a free-kick late ⁠to reduce the deficit.

Mourinho said he could only "hug" his players after what he described as a first half "full of class and great character", but he aimed sharp ‌criticism at referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias and those who appointed him.

"They've put a referee, aged 41, with no international experience - it's certainly not because he's a great referee," Mourinho said.

"Then the poor chap has come ‌here and hasn't been able to cope with the pressure - and it really is intense pressure. I call it '80s-style pressure' here in this stadium, which you hardly ever see these days."

Asked about being six points behind Barcelona, Mourinho offered a pointed reply.

"If they just leave us in peace and let us compete on a level playing field ⁠with everyone else, we've still got a long way to go," he said.

"I don't ​want to go so far as to say this was set up... I ​want to believe that they simply made a mistake."

'A derby marked by poor officiating,' say Real Madrid

Real Madrid released an official match report after full-time which echoed the views of Mourinho.

The La Liga club claimed the defeat was "marked by poor officiating".

"Real Madrid lost at the Metropolitano in a derby marked by the poor officiating of Ortiz Arias, who failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Jude Bellingham's knee (despite reviewing the play on the monitor) and Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

"Both decisions shaped the match, which was decided in the second half in favor of Atletico.

"Until the 30th minute, the game had very few dangerous plays. But from that point on, controversy took over the derby.

"In the 35th minute, during a contested ball, Bellingham got to the ball before Cuti Romero, and the Atletico defender planted his studs into the left knee of the Madrid player. Ortiz Arias initially booked our player but was called by Trujillo Suarez to review the incident on the monitor.

"After watching the replay, he rescinded the card from Bellingham and issued a yellow card to the Atletico defender instead of sending him off.

"Nine minutes later, the referee made another crucial error by not penalizing Kang-In Lee for a challenge on Valverde, where he struck him with his studs on the left ankle.

"Ortiz Arias was close to the incident but did not show a red card (or even a yellow card) to the Atlético player, nor was he alerted by Trujillo Suárez on this occasion."
